claims.statement: LGD-3303 is a nonsteroidal, orally bioavailable SARM that binds the androgen receptor with high in vitro affinity (Ki = 0.9 nM) and potently activates AR-mediated transcription (EC50 = 3.6 nM, 134% efficacy relative to dihydrotestosterone), while showing much weaker affinity for the mineralocorticoid, glucocorticoid, and progesterone receptors (Ki = 1261, 581, and 136 nM respectively).

claims.statement: In castrated male rats (an androgen-deficiency model), oral LGD-3303 at 1 mg/kg/day completely prevented loss of levator ani muscle weight and acted as a partial agonist on prostate and preputial gland tissue; local tissue drug concentrations were reportedly higher in prostate than in the more strongly responding levator ani muscle, indicating the tissue selectivity is not explained by differential drug distribution. This is preclinical rodent evidence only and has not been demonstrated in a human clinical study.

claims.statement: LGD-3303 was originated by Ligand Pharmaceuticals as a candidate SARM investigated for osteoporosis, hypogonadism, and sexual dysfunction. Its highest recorded R&D status is preclinical ("Pending/Preclinical"), all three tracked indications are listed as inactive, and no clinical-trial-phase development is recorded, with the most recent development record dated December 31, 2007. LGD-3303 holds no marketing approval in any jurisdiction, has not entered human clinical trials, and was subsequently encountered outside pharmaceutical development as a novel designer drug by at least 2020.

claims.statement: FDA classifies SARMs as a drug class - which includes LGD-3303 by chemical and pharmacological category - as unapproved products that "cannot be legally marketed in the U.S. as a dietary supplement or drug at this time," and warns that SARM use is associated with increased risk of heart attack or stroke and liver injury/acute liver failure, among other serious effects. No FDA warning letter or enforcement action naming LGD-3303 specifically was located in this session's search of fda.gov.

claims.statement: NIH's LiverTox reference describes a distinctive bland cholestatic drug-induced liver injury pattern documented with SARM use as a class: onset roughly 2-3 months after starting, presenting with fatigue, anorexia, dark urine, and jaundice, with moderate bilirubin elevation (reported 4-8 mg/dL initially) but only 2-5x-normal aminotransferase elevation, and a prolonged but usually self-limited course of about 1-6 months, occasionally with bilirubin cast nephropathy requiring temporary dialysis in severe cases. The compounds specifically named in LiverTox's case-report basis are ligandrol (LGD-4033), enobosarm/ostarine, vosilasarm/RAD-140, andarine, and YK-11; LGD-3303 is not individually named among the documented case reports in this reference, despite sharing the same androgen-receptor mechanism class.

claims.statement: The WADA Prohibited List's S1.2 anabolic-agents category prohibits "Selective androgen receptor modulators [SARMs, e.g. andarine, enobosarm (ostarine), LGD-4033 (ligandrol), RAD140, S-23 and YK-11]" using "including, but not limited to" language, so LGD-3303 falls within the prohibited SARM class as a chemical/pharmacological analog even though it is not individually named in this illustrative list. Independent anti-doping research has developed equine (horse) in vivo metabolite-profiling methods specifically to detect LGD-3303 administration, identifying a monohydroxylated metabolite with better detectability than the parent compound for doping-control testing.

claims.statement: LGD-3303 is sold online by research-chemical vendors carrying explicit "for research use only... not for human use" disclaimers, yet the same vendor product pages foreground preclinical rat muscle-sparing and receptor-potency data (e.g., "completely inhibits the loss of muscle weight," nanomolar Ki/EC50 figures) in ways that read as implied bodybuilding or performance benefit. No human efficacy or safety trial, case series, or FDA/DrugBank clinical data for LGD-3303 was located in this session. Muscle-building, bone-density, or other performance/wellness claims circulating in vendor and forum marketing for LGD-3303 are therefore not supported by human evidence and should not be treated as established benefits.
